GOAL: fix the coupling position for ideation_2 before writing the single proposal.
READ: the round brief (evidence items 1-4 from results/research/issue126 and 121), the list of prior/rejected mechanisms (CURVCTRL-SID, BRad-RQ, poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, behcone-prefix-rq, succboost-geoshift, LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, TSG-SID, BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS), and the workspace (empty: no repo files under the ideation_2 cwd; /fs04/.../121 is outside my permission set).
OBSERVED: three coupling slots are already taken by earlier rounds: (a) per-level curvature driven by prefix-transition score, (b) per-item radial coordinate driven by behaviour entropy/rank, (c) successor-weighted curved Frechet codebook update. Evidence 2 (curvature is a gauge, Poincare saturates above c~2, Lorentz stays sound) and evidence 3 (behaviour-contrast predicts recall, Euclidean control matches or beats plain hyperbolic) rule out any design that estimates curvature, leans on a tree premise, or adds a plain curved distance term beside an unrelated behaviour loss.
REASONING: the only untouched position that is defensible without the tree premise and without estimating c is to use the curvature as a *frame change* (exp/log + parallel transport / gyration) whose base point is a behaviour-defined point, with c fixed at 1 as the gauge and no per-item radius. Behaviour then enters the quantizer through the geodesic DIRECTION of the frame, so no behaviour statistic is used to rank items radially (avoids duplicating BRad-RQ), and removing geometry removes the gyration (a pure Euclidean frame change is only a translation), so the geometry-off arm is structurally, not cosmetically, different.
OPEN AT THIS POINT: the encoder could in principle cancel the frame shift (a_i free), so an explicit content/behaviour orthogonality constraint plus a fixed (constant, not behaviour-ranked) pole radius is needed; also need the per-step cost at 24556 items / 4096 batch / 24 steps

FINAL ANSWER (summary of the one proposal, GYROFRAME-RQ; full text printed in the reply).
Mechanism: the RQ-VAE quantizer keeps curvature c=1 fixed (gauge, never estimated) and keeps a CONSTANT pole radius of one curvature unit for every item, so no behaviour statistic ranks items radially (deliberately outside the BRad-RQ slot) and no per-level curvature is fitted (outside the CURVCTRL-SID slot). Behaviour enters as a DIRECTION only: from training-only session transitions, u_i = sum_j max(0,PMI_ij) t_j - (sum_j max(0,PMI_ij)) t_pop, u_hat_i = u_i/||u_i||, giving base point p_i = exp^c_o(u_hat_i).
Coupling: the quantizer composes from p_i, not from the origin: r_1 = log^c_{p_i}(x_i), and at every level the codebook vector is parallel-transported PT^c_{o->z_{l-1}}(c_{l,k}) before the argmin, so the item-specific GYRATION (a pure curvature effect; the Euclidean frame change at the same cost is only a translation) determines the code index. The encoder output is projected orthogonal to u_hat_i so the encoder cannot cancel the frame shift. SID = the L code indices; the decoder keeps the baseline content reconstruction from log_o(z_L).
Switches (exist, correct, only both-on trained): BEHAV=0 sets u_hat_i=0 -> p_i=o, PT=identity, plain Lorentz RQ; GEOM=0 keeps the pole as a tangent vector and replaces exp/log/PT with plain add/subtract -> behaviour is only a translation.
Why not the refuted premises: no tree/hierarchy premise, no curvature estimation, no plain curved-distance term beside an unrelated loss, and the coupling is inside the assignment and the composition rather than in a side loss.
Cost at the frozen scale: ~9 closed-form Lorentz maps per item per step (O(d), no matrices), ~0.2 GFLOP fwd+bwd per step at batch 4096 and d=64, ~5 GFLOP/epoch, well under 1 percent of the 4-GPU transformer step; one offline pass over train interactions to build n_ij plus a 24556x64 float32 pole buffer (6.3 MB); expected wall clock within 1 percent of the baseline 3000-epoch run.
Observables: level-1 histogram vs the Euclidean-shift variant at init, mean gyration angle, ||<a_i,u_hat_i>|| and ||log_{p_i}(x_i)|| per epoch, train-only prefix successor hit rate and conditional entropy, collisions/distinct-SID count, and finally Stage 3 test_recall@10 (>0.065 the only judgement).
Main risk: the encoder retains second-order freedom to absorb the frame change, which would land the run at baseline recall; that is the go/no-go signature.
